brief: GS's Pasquariello argues breadth is less dire than reported. Though the median S&P stock sits 15% below its 52-week high, the worst reading since the dot-com bubble, most major US indices are up double digits YTD, most sectors and most names are positive, and winners outnumber decliners by a wide margin. He ties this to positioning: a US Portfolio Strategy sentiment gauge has been negative six straight weeks, GS's global prime brokerage net exposure sits in the 10th percentile of the past year, the US market has been net sold three weeks, and client turnover ranks 49th of 52 weeks despite last week's S&P breakout. He expects flows to turn net positive into year end as earnings season builds. Separately, GS forecasts $600bn of 2027 primary issuance against $2tr of buybacks and M&A, though $1.7tr of lockup expirations could push net equity supply to its highest since 2000. His short-term read: tactical setup net positive into October past the midterms, but 2027 looks complicated given decelerating earnings growth, so he stays short fixed income and long NDX, TPX and GSCI. He also flags consumer sentiment is lower now than at the 2009 lows despite a 16-fold S&P return since then.
